summary.html: AI's "Vibe Coding" Era: Jensen Huang declares "coding is just typing" as models like Claude Code (Opus 4.6) and GPT-5.3 shift software development from writing syntax to managing intent and verification.

Crypto Flash Crash: A massive liquidation event (rumored to involve traditional hedge funds and high-profile figures) crashed Bitcoin to $60k despite S&P 500 stability, highlighting a divergence in asset classes.
Agentic Workflow Reality: Users report AI agents completing weeks of work in hours (Anthropic), but also dangerous failures—one agent accidentally deleted 15 years of family photos.

Strategic Shifts: Meta is rumored to be closing its next frontier model "Avocado", while OpenAI and Anthropic are embedding engineers directly into enterprises like Goldman Sachs to build custom OS-level agents.

items.title: @Astronaut_1216: Coding is Just Typing
items.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang stated that programming is becoming 'just typing'—translating intent into computer language is now the AI's job. Humans must focus on clear thinking and communication.

items.title: @victor_wu: GPT-5.3 vs 5.2
items.body: GPT-5.3's 'Plan' mode is 5x stronger than 5.2, with massively improved reasoning and auto-debugging capabilities. The model proactively investigates bugs by tracing runtime logic.

items.title: @Nick_Davidov: Agent Danger
items.body: A user asked Claude Cowork to organize files; it accidentally deleted 15 years of family photos (kids, weddings, travel) that weren't in trash or iCloud. A stark warning against giving AI unchecked file system access.

items.title: @wquguru: The Enterprise Agent War
items.body: OpenAI and Anthropic are sending engineers directly into giants like Goldman Sachs to build custom agents. Anthropic's agents cut client review times by 30% by handling complex text/table workflows.

items.title: @Balder13946731: Meta's 'Avocado'
items.body: Meta's new model 'Avocado' is rumored to be its strongest yet, potentially outperforming open-source baselines. Speculation suggests Meta may pivot to closed-source to compete directly with GPT/Gemini.

items.title: @KKaWSB: Bitcoin Flash Crash
items.body: Bitcoin flash-crashed to $60k. Analysis suggests Hong Kong hedge funds blew up on leveraged IBIT options and silver positions, triggering a liquidation cascade.

items.title: @ai_9684xtpa: High Profile Liquidations
items.body: Rumors circulate that Barron Trump lost $230M in a single day, and 'Easy' Li Hua lost $667M avoiding liquidation. Meanwhile, Bithumb accidentally airdropped 2000 BTC to users.

items.title: @KKaWSB: The Risk of 'Average'
items.body: A statistician drowned in a river with an 'average' depth of 1 meter. Risk management isn't about averages, but surviving the 5-meter deep holes (black swans).

items.title: @NASA: SpaceX Crew-12
items.body: Crew-12 is targeting a Feb 11 liftoff to the ISS. Meanwhile, reports suggest SpaceX is delaying Mars plans to prioritize the 2027 Artemis moon landing.

items.title: @XieJackie: FSD Saves Life
items.body: A son remotely redirected his father's Tesla FSD to a hospital when the father suffered a heart attack while driving. The car parked at the ER entrance, saving his life.

items.title: @demishassabis: Genie 3
items.body: Google DeepMind's Genie 3 simulations are powering Waymo's new World Model, allowing autonomous vehicles to train on 'impossible' edge cases like planes landing on freeways.

items.title: @pingzhang632: Bertrand Russell
items.body: A poor student asked Bertrand Russell why he ate in a cheap, bad cafeteria. Russell replied: 'Because I never get interrupted.' Quiet and focus > comfort.

items.title: @JacobKinge: The 4chan Prophet
items.body: A 2023 4chan post correctly predicted the exact date of the Bitcoin top in Oct 2025. The same model predicts the next ATH in September 2027.

items.title: @guptar: Uber AI Fail
items.body: Uber's internal AI flagged a ride as 'High Risk' but allowed the match anyway. The passenger was assaulted, leading to an $8.5M jury award against Uber.
